newsitem.title: USA: Delta Q4 dampened by excise tax, leisure traffic.
newsitem.headline: Delta Q4 dampened by excise tax, leisure traffic.

text.p: Delta Air Lines Inc said the federal excise tax and growth in less-profitable leisure traffic dampened its fourth quarter results, but the carrier remains "upbeat" about its transatlantic performance and outlook.

"Profits are strong. Costs are under control. Revenues are up. Debt is down. Delta is growing again in a strategic, disciplined way around the world. I have never been more optimistic about this company or its future," said Chairman Ronald Allen, who is to retire when his contract expires on July 31.
"While earnings were down from our record June 1996 quarter, we are pleased that unit costs came in below our expectations and that we continue to see strong demand," Allen said.
For the fourth quarter ended in June, Delta's operating income totaled $519 million, down nine percent from the June 1996 quarter results.
Primary earnings per common share were $3.98, down from $5.77 a year ago. Fully diluted earnings were $3.90 a share, compared to $4.18 a year ago.
Operating revenues increased five percent on three percent higher capacity, due in part to "robust" passenger traffic levels and increased cargo traffic, Delta said.

During the fourth quarter, passenger revenue grew by four percent, driven by a seven percent increase in revenue passenger miles but partially offset by a three percent decline in passenger mile yield.

The decline in passenger mile yield was primarily due to the reimposition on March 7 of the 10 percent transportation excise tax and growth in lower-yielding leisure traffic as a result of competitive pricing actions, Delta said.
Cargo revenue increased nine percent to $143 million on an 18 percent increase in cargo ton miles and an eight percent decline in ton mile yield.

Operating expenses for the June 1997 quarter totaled $3.0 billion, an increase of eight percent from a year ago. Delta said operating expenses increased due to higher staffing levels for customer service initiatives, increased advertising expense for the launch of the enhanced transatlantic business class service, and costs related to higher traffic and revenue levels.
Operating expense per available seat mile increased five percent in the quarter compared with the June 1996 quarter.
Delta's stock was off 15/16 to 87-1/4 in late morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
